principles.text: On a big gap down with no specific catastrophic news, don't panic and don't sell at the open; calm down and evaluate where leaders are relative to their support levels first.
Leaders gapping back into a rising 9 EMA or prior consolidation range is healthy, not bearish; pullbacks let extended names cool off and set up the next leg.
In an uptrend it is better to be too bullish than too bearish; trying to top-tick or pick the top of the move isn't worth it.
Risk roughly 0.3% of account value per position via a defined stop, and let the stops decide the exits.
Buy near the weekly/daily EMAs while a stock is still within its base/range; fast markets give less consolidation so don't miss the breakout waiting for a perfect pullback.
Getting stopped out in the first minute or two after the open is acceptable; if a name gaps into a support level near your stop you can simply re-buy it when you like the action.
Learn to sit tight and let the stock guide the trade; experiencing repeated shakeouts that then find support teaches you to hold instead of leaving the trade to the market.
Markets usually give warning signs and a choppy digestion period before a real top/crack; trust the trend and momentum until something strange shows up.
